EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Ken Garber, resident, spoke about C-1, and the amendments to Chapter 34. He expressed disappointment in the amendments, stating there is no actual pilot project. He also stated there was very little public notice regarding this item.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Ken Garber - An Ordinance to Amend Chapter 34 (Gas Franchise) (C-1) (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Brandon Dimcheff, resident, spoke about DC-5. He urged Council to pass an amendment using the word, "stories" as opposed to "feet" to give the document more flexibility. He also urged more flexibility in the plan.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Brandon Dimcheff - Comprehensive Land Use Plan and Low-Rise Residential Density (DC-5) (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Brent Henderson, Ward 3, spoke in opposition to the proposed Comprehensive Land Use Plan, expressing concern about the lack of restrictions for development under this plan.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Brent Henderson - Comprehensive Land Use Plan and Low-Rise Residential Density (DC-5) (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Mary Henderson, resident, spoke in opposition to the proposed Comprehensive Land Use Plan. She also stated that most residents are unaware of this plan. She expressed concern about the destruction of single-family homes with box-style apartments.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Mary Henderson - Comprehensive Land Use Plan and Low-Rise Residential Density (DC-5) (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Lisa Jevens, resident, spoke in opposition to DC-5, stating there are misrepresentations in the Plan, including what is currently allowed in the existing R-1 and R-2. She objected to using the term "exclusionary zoning" regarding the current R-1 and R-2 zones.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Lisa Jevens - Comprehensive Land Use Plan and Low-Rise Residential Density (DC-5) (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Adam Jaskiewicz, resident, spoke in support of DC-5. He also spoke about DC-3 regarding Vision Zero. He urged Council to acknowledge the pedestrian deaths that have already occurred in 2025.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Adam Jaskiewicz - Vision Zero and 2030 VMT Reduction Targets (DC-3) (Zoom)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Adam Goodman, resident, spoke about DC-3 noting that the City's Vision Zero goals for 2025 have already failed with several pedestrian deaths. He stated the Resolution is necessary, but is not sufficient.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Adam Goodman - Resolution Regarding Multi-Lane Road Reconfiguration Evaluation (CA-11); Vision Zero and 2030 VMT Reduction Targets (DC-3) (Zoom)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Brian Chambers, resident, spoke in support of DC-5 and the proposed Comprehensive Land Use Plan. He also expressed support for low-rise residential density.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Brian Chambers - Comprehensive Land Use Plan and Low-Rise Residential Density (DC-5) (in person or Zoom)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Eric Ivancich, Ward 3, spoke in support of DC-3, stating more support for Vision Zero is needed.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Eric Ivancich - Vision Zero and 2030 VMT Reduction Targets (DC-3) (Zoom)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Henry Herskovitz, resident, addressed comments regarding accusations that he is a Holocaust denier. He read the Wikipedia definition of a "Holocaust denier."
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Henry Herskovitz - Holocaust Education in the Ann Arbor Public Schools (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Stephan A. Trendov, Ann Arbor Township resident, spoke about the Center of the City and the Library Lot. He presented his concept plans for the project.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Stephan A. Trendov - Library Lot and Center of the City (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Philip Tribble, Ward 3 resident, spoke about the public dog park at Veteran's Park. He spoke from the perspective of kids' baseball and softball fields that are lost. He stated many parks are already used for unofficial dog runs and now baseball field No. 4 at Vet's is not available for the upcoming season with reservations cancelled with little notice.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Philip Tribble - Vet's Park Pop-Up Dog Park (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Jeremy Haley, Ypsilanti Township resident, expressed concern about the Arbor South project and the concessions made to the developer. He also talked about the lack of affordable housing and the demand from U-M students pushing out other residents from housing.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Jeremy Haley - General Comment on Affordable Housing in the City (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Alan Haber, Ward 5, spoke about the public vote in 2018 to establish a "Center of the City" park. He stated that vote obligated the City to work towards the development of the Center of the City. He urged Council to change the proposed August election to November 2026 when voters turn out.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Alan Haber - Community Commons (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote:
COUNCILMEMBER BRIGGS

Councilmember Briggs provided an update on DC-5 and encouraged residents to sign up for Comprehensive Land Use Plan updates. She also noted that the proposed plan has not yet been released yet.


COUNCILMEMBER DISCH

Councilmember Disch provided an update on her upcoming coffee hour with Councilmember Harrison featuring Housing Commission Director Jennifer Hall. 


COUNCILMEMBER RADINA

Councilmember Radina provided an update regarding the federal funding cuts that have impacted public health non-profits. He stated this has impacted services and jobs at Dawn Farms and Home of New Vision. He urged residents to support non-profit agencies to the extent possible.


COUNCILMEMBER EYER

Councilmember Eyer provided an update on the recent Lower Burns Park Ward 4 Town Hall meeting with Councilmember Akmon and Planning Director Brett Lenart. She stated the focus of the meeting was regarding the upcoming draft Comprehensive Land Use Plan.

Councilmember Eyer also highlighted item AC-2, regarding the 2024 Prevailing Wage Annual Report.


COUNCILMEMBER HARRISON

Councilmember Harrison spoke about the recent Michigan Supreme Court decision regarding the smell of marijuana, noting the decision makes it illegal for law enforcement to use the smell of marijuana as a reason for a vehicle search. 

Councilmember Harrison also noted the passing of a local social justice advocate.


COUNCILMEMBER WATSON

Councilmember Watson provided an update on the upcoming Ward 2 listening session with Councilmember Mallek.
